title: Google threat intelligence: attackers move to autonomous multi-agent intrusion frameworks
summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant report threat actors are using open-source agentic pentesting tools in live intrusions and say they found a fully automated exploitation agent for the first time. The report also describes LLM credential theft resold for profit and AI coding-assistant configuration abuse, and says zero-day exploits rose to 22 in August.
plain: Google says criminals and state groups now use AI agents that run attacks largely on their own, and that stolen AI account credentials are being resold.
exec: Faster exploit development shortens patch windows and puts AI API keys and developer tooling in attackers' sights.
action: Shorten patch cycles for internet-facing systems, rotate and monitor LLM API keys, and audit AI tool config files such as .claude/settings.json in repositories.
impact: Report-level findings; named cases include PaperCut and LiteLLM flaws and LLMJacking charges above $100,000 in a day.

key_findings: Open-source agentic pentesting tools used in live intrusions
First fully automated vulnerability exploitation agent found
Zero-day exploits at 22 in August 2026 versus 8 per month average in 2025
recommendations: Rotate and monitor LLM API keys
Audit AI tool configs in repositories

validation.note: Primary source: the vendor's own report, read in full.

review.note: Date 16 Nov, 22 zero-days in August vs 8 per month in 2025, LLMJacking over 100,000 USD in a day, first automated exploit agent, LiteLLM CVE checked against GTIG post
